messages:
mira: gpu-health-bot just opened alerts for an ECC/Xid burst across 3 nodes in us-west2-a (repeat Xid 65 on two). Seeing a handful of transient CUDA OOMs in pods. I'm leaning towards a 'soft quarantine' flow: cordon + annotated live-evict with extended grace rather than instant hard drain. Less risk of thundering re-schedules for latency-sensitive services. Thoughts?

gpu-health-bot: ALERT: node gpu-uw2-a-12 | ECC_ERR_RATE spike (5m) -> +420% | Xid 65 repeats: 2/3 devices. Linked: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/gpu-health?orgId=1&var-node=gpu-uw2-a-12

sam: +1 for soft quarantine. Our hysteresis is still short for Xid bursts. What exact metric should trigger the quarantine vs full drain? ecc_errors_per_min or repeated Xid counters?

mira: thinking: trigger on (Xid repeat count >=2 within 10m) OR (ECC uncorrectable per-min > 2) and then start soft quarantine window = 30m. If errors persist -> escalate to full drain.

gwen: can we list the nodes and which pods would be affected? I saw two long-running batch pods on gpu-uw2-a-12. node names: gpu-uw2-a-12, gpu-uw2-a-18, gpu-uw2-a-21.

kai: rough flow idea: annotate node as quarantined, adjust scheduler affinity to avoid scheduling new latency-sensitive pods there, then gently evict tolerant/prefetchable pods respecting PDBs. Something like:
```
kubectl annotate node gpu-uw2-a-12 redwood/evict-mode=soft
kubectl cordon gpu-uw2-a-12
# Evict non-critical pods with longer grace and respect PDBs via eviction API
```
We need a confirmer job that watches for Xid recurrence during the 30m window.

oliver: also ensure cluster-autoscaler doesn't immediately spin up more nodes and push batch there. We should tag quarantined nodes so autoscaler treats them as unschedulable for the first 30m. Otherwise we just shuffle work.

ada: for Slurm tenants: we should requeue running jobs that are checkpointable and politely drain the rest. Eg: use `scontrol update NodeName=gpu-uw2-a-12 State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-quarantine"` then `squeue`/`sacct` to decide requeue vs requeue+checkpoint.

oncall: i'm oncall, will coordinate the live quarantine. i'll run the initial cordon and the first-pass evictions, then monitor logs and smi. Ping me when ready.

mira: thanks. plan of action -> 1) oncall annotates & cordons 2) infra tooling runs eviction playbook with 30m observation window 3) if Xid/ECC still firing -> promote to full drain and replacement 4) open a ticket to adjust thresholds + add canary test. i'll write the playbook and link it here.

sam: small ask: add a short canary to the infra CI that simulates a flakey GPU (increment Xid metric) so we can validate soft quarantine doesn't cause regressions.

kai: yeah, add a simple repro harness `gpu-err-injector` in sandbox pool. we can run it once we merge the playbook.

gwen: during the quarantine window, let's route latency-sensitive inference traffic away from the AZ (temporary routing policy). That buys time without killing jobs.

mira: agreed. i'll update the routing policy and the runbook. runbook draft: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-temporal-quarantine (WIP). PR for playbook in infra repo coming shortly: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1234

oncall: cordon & annotate done for gpu-uw2-a-12. starting evictions (long grace). monitoring logs now. will report back in 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ada: requeue policy executed for Slurm jobs on that node; one job checkpointed and requeued, two jobs ineligible (not checkpointable) were politely migrated when possible.

sam: :thumbsup: thanks all. postmortem/monitoring follow-up: add a dashboard panel for Xid repeat counts and a small alert that suggests soft quarantine instead of immediate drain.

mira: agreed. closing the loop after postmortem. thanks oncall and team. :heart:
